memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "It has always been my ambition to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation." — Romans 15:20

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
There is a comfortable temptation to keep our "fishing" limited to the familiar waters of the fish tank, focusing our efforts only on those who already sit within our pews or live within our immediate circles. While tending the flock is necessary, the Great Commission calls for a more adventurous spirit. A fish tank is a closed system, but the world is a vast ocean. We are called to be fishers of men who venture into the "deep," seeking out the places where the Gospel has yet to break the surface of daily life.
​The Apostle Paul sets the ultimate precedent for this mission. He intentionally bypassed regions where the foundation of Christ had already been laid, choosing instead to advance toward the unreached. He understood that the Kingdom of God does not expand by simply rearranging the fish within a tank; it grows when we cast our nets into the deep, unknown waters. The world is far too vast for a small, stationary group to impact. We must adopt a global vision that refuses to settle for the safety of the shallows.
​Today, the call to "Go" is a mandate that can be fulfilled in various ways. Not everyone is called to cross an ocean, but everyone is called to participate in the harvest. If you cannot go yourself, you are called to appoint, send, or sacrificially support those who can. Whether through your feet, your prayers, or your resources, your "net" must reach beyond the familiar. We must stop competing for the same small space and start laboring for the vast, unreached territory that is still waiting for the Light.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "God isn't looking for people of great faith, but for individuals ready to follow a great God." — Hudson Taylor

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, break my heart for what breaks Yours. Forgive me for staying in the safety of the "fish tank" when You have called me to the depths of the sea. Grant me the courage of Paul to look toward the unreached. Whether I go, send, or support, let my life be a tool for the expansion of Your Kingdom. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Your comfort zone is often the greatest enemy of your calling. Don't be afraid to cast your net where no one else is looking.
